resources.string: Real-time DFA a1 is calculated over a rolling 2-minute window (updated every 5 seconds) and rMSSD over 60 seconds. Rapid pacing changes take 1–2 minutes to manifest in autonomic telemetry.
Accurate beat-to-beat RR intervals require a moistened ECG chest strap (such as Polar H10 or Garmin HRM-Pro). Optical wrist sensors smooth interval timings and are unsuitable for DFA a1.

DFA a1 > 0.75 indicates aerobic endurance pacing (Zone 2). Values between 0.75 and 0.50 reflect the aerobic-anaerobic threshold transition (Zone 3). Values below 0.50 indicate high anaerobic intensity (Zone 4).
Autonomic HRV metrics in aTrainingTracker are designed for athletic training guidance and do not replace medical evaluation. Cardiac arrhythmias or ectopic beats may invalidate threshold estimates.
